verdict.rationale: Highnote documents a first-party Card Viewer SDK that embeds sensitive card data in the developer's UI via iframes, so PCI-scoped data never flows through the developer's servers or reaches page scripts. Its PCI guidance tells subscribers to use the SDKs to reduce compliance requirements. That is the core hosted-component reveal flow, but the docs only say 'reduce' and never name SAQ D or a lighter SAQ level. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that PAN and CVV specifically are displayed, a vendor statement that the integration keeps you out of SAQ D (or names the resulting SAQ level), ephemeral-key reveal flow details, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can show cardholders their own PAN and CVV without inheriting PCI scope — hosted components or ephemeral-key reveal flows the vendor documents as keeping me out of SAQ D

citations.quote: The Highnote Card Viewer SDK lets you embed sensitive card data into your UI using iframes. This prevents PCI-scoped data from flowing through your servers or from being accessible to scripts running on your page.
Consider using the Highnote SDKs to reduce your PCI compliance requirements.
Embed sensitive card data in your UI and avoid PCI data from being compromised
